title: Ehrlichiosis: morulae in monocytes (Ehrlichia chaffeensis)
vignette: A 32-year-old man comes to the office due to an acute febrile illness that developed after a deer-hunting trip in Arkansas. The patient recalls getting tick bites in the woods but initially had no symptoms. He began experiencing fever, chills, malaise, headache, and myalgia a week after his return. Physical examination shows a diffuse, maculopapular rash; clear oropharynx; normal lung and heart sounds; and mild, diffuse abdominal tenderness. Laboratory testing reveals leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated aminotransferase levels. Microscopic evaluation of the blood demonstrates mulberry-shaped, intracytoplasmic inclusions (morulae) in monocytes. Which of the following is the most likely pathogen responsible for this patient's condition?

clues.note: The southeastern/south-central US and white-tailed deer/tick exposure are the setting for ehrlichiosis (lone star tick).

clues.text: leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated aminotransferase levels
clues.note: Leukopenia + thrombocytopenia + transaminitis are the characteristic lab abnormalities of ehrlichiosis (and anaplasmosis).
MORULAE (mulberry-like inclusions) inside MONOCYTES are diagnostic of Ehrlichia chaffeensis (human monocytic ehrlichiosis).

whatMatters: Tick exposure in the south-central US + fever + leukopenia/thrombocytopenia/transaminitis + MORULAE in MONOCYTES = human monocytic ehrlichiosis, caused by EHRLICHIA CHAFFEENSIS (harbored in white-tailed deer, transmitted by the lone star tick). Answer C. Treat with doxycycline.
strategy: Anchor on the pathognomonic finding: morulae (intracytoplasmic mulberry inclusions) in MONOCYTES = Ehrlichia (in granulocytes/neutrophils = Anaplasma). Combined with the geography, cytopenias, and transaminitis, it's Ehrlichia chaffeensis. Reject Babesia (intraerythrocytic ring/Maltese cross), Borrelia (Lyme - erythema migrans, not seen on smear), Francisella (tularemia - ulcer + lymphadenopathy), and Rickettsia rickettsii (Rocky Mountain spotted fever - rash on wrists/ankles, endothelial cells).

eliminations.label: Babesia microti - intraerythrocytic rings (not monocytes)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a protozoan causing babesiosis (northeastern US, Ixodes tick) with ring-shaped, intraERYTHROCYTIC parasites and a Maltese cross. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: Babesia is inside RED cells, not the intraMONOCYTIC morulae here. ✅ Correct if: intraerythrocytic rings/Maltese cross with hemolysis.

eliminations.label: Borrelia burgdorferi - Lyme (erythema migrans, not on smear)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the Lyme disease spirochete (Ixodes tick). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes erythema migrans and is not typically visualized on a blood smear or seen as morulae in monocytes. ✅ Correct if: target-shaped erythema migrans rash.

eliminations.label: Francisella tularensis - tularemia (ulcer + lymphadenopathy)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a gram-negative bacterium (from rabbits/ticks) causing tularemia with an ulcer and regional lymphadenopathy. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it does not form intramonocytic morulae. ✅ Correct if: ulceroglandular disease with an eschar-like ulcer.

eliminations.label: Rickettsia rickettsii - Rocky Mountain spotted fever (endothelium)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the RMSF organism, invading vascular ENDOTHELIAL cells, causing a petechial rash spreading from wrists/ankles. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it targets endothelium (not monocyte morulae); the rash pattern differs. ✅ Correct if: centripetal rash from wrists/ankles after Dermacentor tick.

reasoning: Tick exposure in Arkansas + febrile illness + leukopenia/thrombocytopenia/transaminitis
Blood smear shows morulae (mulberry inclusions) in MONOCYTES
Morulae in monocytes = human monocytic ehrlichiosis (Ehrlichia chaffeensis)
mechanism: Ehrlichia chaffeensis is an obligate intracellular bacterium harbored by WHITE-TAILED DEER and transmitted to humans by the LONE STAR TICK (Amblyomma americanum) in the southeastern, southeastern, and mid-Atlantic/south-central US. It replicates within membrane-bound vacuoles in the CYTOPLASM OF MONOCYTES, forming clusters called MORULAE - mulberry-shaped INTRACYTOPLASMIC INCLUSIONS visible on peripheral blood/buffy-coat smears. About a week after the bite, patients develop a nonspecific febrile illness (fever, chills, headache, myalgia), often with a maculopapular rash, and characteristic laboratory abnormalities: LEUKOPENIA, THROMBOCYTOPENIA, and elevated AMINOTRANSFERASES. Human granulocytic ANAPLASMOSIS (Anaplasma phagocytophilum) is a related tick-borne illness with morulae in GRANULOCYTES/neutrophils instead. Treatment is doxycycline (empiric, even before confirmation). The distractors are other tick-borne diseases distinguished by their organisms/findings: Babesia (intraerythrocytic rings), Borrelia (Lyme/erythema migrans), Francisella (tularemia ulcer), and Rickettsia rickettsii (RMSF, endothelial infection with a wrist/ankle rash).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > ehrlichiosis: Ehrlichia chaffeensis, lone star tick, white-tailed deer; morulae in MONOCYTES; leukopenia/thrombocytopenia/transaminitis; doxycycline. Anaplasma = morulae in granulocytes.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Morulae in MONOCYTES + cytopenias = Ehrlichia chaffeensis (monocytic ehrlichiosis).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on morula, monocyte vs granulocyte, ehrlichiosis vs anaplasmosis, or lone star tick? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Babesia = intraerythrocytic rings; Borrelia = erythema migrans; Francisella = ulcer/lymphadenopathy; RMSF = endothelium/wrist-ankle rash.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: Ehrlichia = morulae in monocytes; Anaplasma = morulae in granulocytes; both -> cytopenias/transaminitis; treat doxycycline.

keywords.front: Morulae in MONOCYTES + cytopenias + tick exposure

firstAid.detail: Micro: Ehrlichia chaffeensis; morulae in monocytes; cytopenias; doxycycline.
Micro > Babesia (RBC rings), Borrelia (Lyme), Francisella (tularemia), RMSF.

memoryHook: Ehrlichia hides mulberry morulae in MONOcytes (Ehrlichia = 'E for Eating monocytes'); Anaplasma picks granulocytes - both drop the counts and both bow to doxycycline.
